"""Parse access-log lines of the form:

    2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00 GET /api/items 200 123ms
"""
from datetime import datetime


def parse_line(line):
    parts = line.split()
    ts = datetime.strptime(parts[0][:19], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
    return {
        "time": ts,
        "method": parts[1],
        "path": parts[2],
        "status": int(parts[3]),
        "latency_ms": int(parts[4].rstrip("ms")),
    }


def p95_latency(lines):
    values = sorted(parse_line(l)["latency_ms"] for l in lines)
    return values[int(len(values) * 0.95)]

import unittest
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from logstats.parser import parse_line, p95_latency


def line(latency_ms, ts="2026-10-01T12:00:00Z"):
    return f"{ts} GET /api/items 200 {latency_ms}ms"


class TimestampTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_z_is_utc(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 10, 1, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_positive_offset_converted_to_utc(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00 GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"].tzinfo, timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 10, 1, 9, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_negative_offset_converted_to_utc(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00-05:00 GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"].tzinfo, timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 10, 1, 17, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_offset_crossing_day_boundary(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T00:30:00+03:00 GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 9, 30, 21, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_timestamp_without_offset_assumed_utc(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00 GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"].tzinfo, timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 10, 1, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_fields_are_parsed(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00 POST /a 404 17ms")
        self.assertEqual(
            {k: r[k] for k in ("method", "path", "status", "latency_ms")},
            {"method": "POST", "path": "/a", "status": 404, "latency_ms": 17},
        )


class MalformedLineTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_all_malformed_lines_raise_value_error(self):
        bad_lines = [
            "",
            "   ",
            "garbage",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a 200",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a 200 15ms extra",
            "not-a-timestamp GET /a 200 15ms",
            "2026-13-45T99:99:99Z GET /a 200 15ms",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a abc 15ms",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a 200 fast",
            None,
            42,
        ]
        for bad in bad_lines:
            with self.subTest(line=bad):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    parse_line(bad)

    def test_empty_input_raises_value_error(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            p95_latency([])

        self.assertEqual(p95_latency([line(42)]), 42)

        self.assertEqual(p95_latency([line(v) for v in range(1, 11)]), 10)

"""Parse access-log lines of the form:

    2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00 GET /api/items 200 123ms
"""
from datetime import datetime


def parse_line(line):
    parts = line.split()
    ts = datetime.strptime(parts[0][:19], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
    return {
        "time": ts,
        "method": parts[1],
        "path": parts[2],
        "status": int(parts[3]),
        "latency_ms": int(parts[4].rstrip("ms")),
    }


def p95_latency(lines):

"""Parse access-log lines of the form:

    2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00 GET /api/items 200 123ms

The timestamp may carry an explicit UTC offset (``+03:00``) or the UTC
designator ``Z``.  It is always normalised to a timezone-aware datetime in
UTC; timestamps given without an offset are assumed to already be UTC.
"""
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# A valid line has exactly: <timestamp> <method> <path> <status> <latency>
FIELD_COUNT = 5

_TIMESTAMP_FORMATS = (
    # (format, offset_aware) - tried in order, first match wins.
    ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z", True),
    ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z", True),
    ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", False),
    ("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f", False),
)


def parse_line(line):
    """Parse a single access-log line into a dict.

    The returned "time" value is always a timezone-aware datetime in UTC.

    Raises ValueError (with a helpful message) for malformed lines.
    """
    if not isinstance(line, str):
        raise ValueError(f"expected a log line of type str, got {type(line).__name__}")

    parts = line.split()
    if len(parts) != FIELD_COUNT:
        raise ValueError(
            f"malformed log line (expected {FIELD_COUNT} fields, got "
            f"{len(parts)}): {line!r}"
        )

    timestamp = _parse_timestamp(parts[0], line)

    try:
        status = int(parts[3])
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed status code {parts[3]!r} in line {line!r}") from None

    return {
        "time": timestamp,
        "method": parts[1],
        "path": parts[2],
        "status": status,
        "latency_ms": _parse_latency_ms(parts[4], line),
    }


def p95_latency(lines):
    """Return the 95th percentile latency (ms) of the given log lines.

    Uses the nearest-rank method: the latencies are sorted and the value at
    1-based rank ceil(0.95 * n) is returned.

    Raises ValueError if there are no samples.
    """
    values = sorted(parse_line(line)["latency_ms"] for line in lines)
    if not values:
        raise ValueError("p95_latency() requires at least one sample")

    # Nearest-rank, 1-based.  0.95 is exactly 19/20, so the rank is computed
    # with integer arithmetic to avoid binary floating-point drift.
    rank = -(-19 * len(values) // 20)
    return values[rank - 1]


def _parse_timestamp(token, line):
    """Parse the timestamp field and normalise it to an aware UTC datetime.

    Timestamps with a UTC offset are converted to UTC; timestamps given
    without an offset are assumed to already be UTC.
    """
    # Normalise the 'Z' designator to an explicit offset so parsing does not
    # depend on strptime's (newer) support for it.
    text = token[:-1] + "+00:00" if token.endswith("Z") else token

    for fmt, offset_aware in _TIMESTAMP_FORMATS:
        try:
            timestamp = datetime.strptime(text, fmt)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if not offset_aware:
            return timestamp.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        return timestamp.astimezone(timezone.utc)

    raise ValueError(f"malformed timestamp {token!r} in line {line!r}")


def _parse_latency_ms(token, line):
    """Parse the latency field (e.g. '123ms') as an int number of milliseconds."""
    text = token[: -len("ms")] if token.endswith("ms") else token
    try:
        return int(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f"malformed latency {token!r} in line {line!r}") from None

        self.assertEqual(r["time"].tzinfo, timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 10, 1, 9, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_negative_offset_converted_to_utc(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00-05:00 GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"].tzinfo, timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 10, 1, 17, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_offset_crossing_day_boundary(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T00:30:00+03:00 GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 9, 30, 21, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_timestamp_without_offset_assumed_utc(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00 GET /a 200 15ms")
        self.assertEqual(r["time"].tzinfo, timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(r["time"], datetime(2026, 10, 1, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_fields_are_parsed(self):
        r = parse_line("2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00 POST /a 404 17ms")
        self.assertEqual(
            {k: r[k] for k in ("method", "path", "status", "latency_ms")},
            {"method": "POST", "path": "/a", "status": 404, "latency_ms": 17},
        )


class MalformedLineTest(unittest.TestCase):

            "   ",
            "garbage",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a 200",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a 200 15ms extra",
            "not-a-timestamp GET /a 200 15ms",
            "2026-13-45T99:99:99Z GET /a 200 15ms",
            "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z GET /a abc 15ms",
